plants.name: Tropical Hibiscus
plants.idNote: Braided-trunk standard; blooms red on the porch.

care.light: Full sun to bright part sun, 6+ hours
care.water: Keep evenly moist; container dries fast in summer heat
care.catNote: ASPCA lists hibiscus (Rose of China) as non-toxic to cats.
care.note: Each bloom lasts about a day; bring indoors before fall frost in the Northeast.

care.humidity: High (60%+); browns at edges in dry air
care.light: Bright indirect light; avoid harsh direct sun
care.water: Keep consistently moist; water when top 2-3 cm dry
care.catNote: Toxic to cats per ASPCA (sapogenins); berries cause GI upset, contact dermatitis
care.note: Not a true fern, it's an asparagus relative with tiny hidden thorns on mature stems

plants.name: Hens & Chicks
plants.idNote: Fuzzy-edged rosette; exact species uncertain.

care.light: Full sun to bright light
care.water: Drench when soil is fully dry; barely in winter
care.catNote: Non-toxic to cats per ASPCA.
care.note: Each rosette dies after flowering, but its 'chicks' carry on.

plants.name: Crinkle-Leaf Plant
plants.idNote: Sending up a flower stalk!

care.light: Bright light with some direct sun
care.water: Soak when dry; much less in winter
care.catNote: Not on the ASPCA list - a jade relative, so best kept from nibblers.
care.note: Leaves snap off easily and can root into whole new plants.

plants.name: Hybrid Aloe
plants.idNote: Red-toothed hybrid aloe; 'Christmas Carol' is our best match.

care.humidity: Low - average room air is fine
care.light: Bright light; sun deepens the red color
care.water: Water deeply only when soil is fully dry
care.catNote: Aloes are toxic to cats per ASPCA (vomiting, lethargy).
care.note: Sun stress and cool nights turn it ruby red.

care.humidity: Moderate; tolerates ~45% if soil stays moist
care.light: Bright indirect light to part shade
care.water: Keep soil evenly moist, not soggy
care.catNote: Non-toxic to cats per ASPCA (Pilea microphylla listed as safe)
care.note: Named for flowers that explosively fire pollen in little puffs when touched

care.light: As much direct sun as possible
care.water: Very sparingly; none while splitting or in winter
care.catNote: Mesembs are generally non-toxic to cats.
care.note: Overwatering makes it burst - it should hold only one leaf pair at a time.

care.light: Bright sun on a windowsill
care.water: Lightly in spring/fall; keep dry in summer heat and winter
care.catNote: Non-toxic to cats (mesemb family, generally pet-safe).
care.note: In habitat it grows buried, with only its clear leaf 'windows' above the sand.

care.light: Bright indirect; tolerates less sun than most succulents
care.water: When fully dry, roughly every 2-3 weeks
care.catNote: Haworthia are non-toxic to cats per ASPCA.
care.note: One of the best succulents for windows without full sun.

care.light: Bright indirect light; tolerates some shade
care.water: Soak when dry; sparingly in winter
care.catNote: Gasteria are commonly listed as pet-safe (non-toxic).
care.note: Named for its little stomach-shaped flowers.

care.humidity: Average home humidity fine; a bit extra keeps tips green
care.light: Bright indirect; purple stripes fade in low light
care.water: Let top 2-3 cm dry between waterings
care.catNote: Toxic to cats per ASPCA inch plant listing; sap causes dermatitis and GI upset
care.note: Grows an inch at a time; pinch stem tips often to keep it bushy instead of leggy

care.humidity: Average; thrives in warm humid summers
care.light: Full sun
care.water: Evenly moist; tolerates brief dry spells
care.catNote: Not on ASPCA lists but widely reported non-toxic to cats, dogs, and people.
care.note: Star-shaped flower clusters are butterfly favorites; deadhead to keep blooms coming all season.

care.light: Full sun to bright light
care.water: Soak-and-dry in summer; nearly dry in winter
care.catNote: Not known to be toxic to cats.
care.note: The 'teeth' are soft - in habitat they help collect fog moisture.

plants.name: Eve's Needle Cactus
plants.idNote: Knobby stems with tiny leaf tufts; could also be a corncob euphorbia.

care.light: Full sun
care.water: Water when fully dry; roughly monthly
care.catNote: Not toxic to cats, but the spines are a real physical hazard.
care.note: In the Andes it grows into a four-meter tree.

plants.name: Mystery Mesemb
plants.idNote: Smooth paired 'fingers' - our best guess is a Cheiridopsis.

care.light: Bright sun
care.water: Winter grower: water fall-spring, keep mostly dry in summer
care.catNote: Mesembs are generally pet-safe, but our ID is uncertain.
care.note: A South African winter grower - its seasons run opposite ours.

plants.name: Variegated String of Buttons
plants.idNote: Nursery label reads 'Crassula perforata variegata'.

care.light: Bright light with some direct sun
care.water: Soak when dry; eases off in midsummer
care.catNote: Crassula (jade family) are toxic to cats per ASPCA.
care.note: The stems look threaded straight through the stacked leaves.

care.light: Bright light to full sun
care.water: Water when dry spring-fall; sparingly in winter
care.catNote: Euphorbia sap is toxic and irritating to cats per ASPCA.
care.note: The milky sap irritates human skin too - gloves on for repotting.

plants.name: Anise Hyssop
plants.idNote: Flower spikes drying - seeds incoming?

care.light: Full sun to part shade, 6+ hours best
care.water: Water when soil dries a few inches down; drought tolerant once established
care.catNote: Not on the ASPCA toxic list; widely regarded as non-toxic to cats.
care.note: Licorice-scented leaves make good tea, and blooms are a bee and hummingbird magnet.

plants.name: Coleus
plants.idNote: Came with its own COLEUS tag.

care.light: Part shade to bright indirect; morning sun is ideal
care.water: Keep evenly moist; water when top inch feels dry
care.catNote: ASPCA lists coleus as toxic to cats; essential oils cause vomiting and diarrhea.
care.note: Pinch off flower spikes so energy goes into its vividly colored foliage.

care.humidity: Prefers dry air with good airflow
care.light: Full sun, 6+ hours
care.water: Water when top inch is dry; never let pot sit in water
care.catNote: ASPCA lists rosemary as non-toxic to cats.
care.note: Overwatering is the top killer of potted rosemary; sharp drainage is essential.

plants.name: Mystery Seedling
plants.idNote: Pinnate baby leaves - best guess is a tamarind sprouted from seed.

care.humidity: High, 60%+; mist or use a humidifier
care.light: Bright direct sun; south window, 6+ hours
care.water: Keep seedling evenly moist; later water when top 1-2 inches dry
care.catNote: Not on the ASPCA toxic list; tamarind is generally considered non-toxic to cats.
care.note: Soak seeds 12-24 hours before sowing; keep it warm (70-80F) away from cold drafts.

care.light: Full sun, 6-8 hours; won't bloom in shade
care.water: Drought tolerant; one deep watering a week in summer
care.catNote: ASPCA lists moss rose (Portulaca) as toxic to cats via soluble calcium oxalates.
care.note: Succulent leaves store water, and flowers close at night and on cloudy days.

plants.name: Spider Plant Cutting
plants.idNote: Rooting in water - likely a pup of the big curly spider plant.

care.light: Medium to bright indirect; avoid direct midday sun
care.water: Let top 2-5 cm dry between waterings
care.catNote: Non-toxic to cats per ASPCA, though cats love chewing it and may get mild GI upset
care.note: Fluoride in tap water causes brown tips; 'Bonnie' has fun curly leaves and makes babies

care.light: 6+ hours of bright indirect light
care.water: When top inch dries; drain the foil sleeve
care.catNote: Mildly toxic per ASPCA; sap irritates mouth and stomach, though its danger is often overrated.
care.note: Needs about 14 hours of total darkness nightly for 8 weeks in fall to re-color its bracts.

care.light: Bright direct light, 4+ hours daily
care.water: Soak and dry; barely water in winter
care.catNote: Not on ASPCA toxic list; Mammillaria cacti are non-toxic, though spines pose a poke hazard.
care.note: Its folded brain shape comes from a rare crested mutation of the ladyfinger cactus.

care.humidity: High; most homes too dry, use humidifier or pebble tray
care.light: Bright filtered/indirect light; direct sun burns fronds
care.water: Keep soil evenly moist; water when surface starts to dry
care.catNote: Non-toxic to cats per ASPCA (a true fern, safe to nibble)
care.note: Sheds and browns in dry winter air; regular misting or a bathroom spot keeps it lush

plants.name: Poinsettia (Big One)
plants.idNote: Survived the holidays and thriving.

care.light: 6+ hours of bright indirect light
care.water: When top inch dries; drain the foil sleeve
care.catNote: Mildly toxic per ASPCA; sap irritates mouth and stomach, though its danger is often overrated.
care.note: Needs about 14 hours of total darkness nightly for 8 weeks in fall to re-color its bracts.

plants.name: Lavender
plants.idNote: Looking crispy on the porch - fingers crossed.

care.humidity: Needs dry air; dislikes humid, stagnant spots
care.light: Full sun, 6-8 hours
care.water: Sparingly; let soil dry out, hates wet feet
care.catNote: ASPCA lists lavender as toxic to cats; linalool causes nausea and vomiting.
care.note: Use lean gritty mix in an unglazed pot; humid Northeast summers invite fungal issues.

plants.name: Spider Flower
plants.idNote: Hairy stems + palmate leaves; best guess is cleome.

care.light: Full sun
care.water: Let soil dry slightly between waterings; drought tolerant once established
care.catNote: ASPCA lists spider flower as non-toxic to cats.
care.note: Self-sows readily and deadheads itself; older varieties have thorny, musky stems.

care.light: Bright indirect; direct sun scorches cream patches
care.water: Water when top 2-3 cm dry; never soggy
care.catNote: Toxic to cats per ASPCA (insoluble calcium oxalates), listed as Swiss cheese plant
care.note: Tissue-culture variegation is stable, but white areas lack chlorophyll so it grows slowly

care.light: Low to bright indirect; variegation fades in dim spots
care.water: Let top 2-5 cm dry between waterings
care.catNote: Toxic to cats per ASPCA (insoluble calcium oxalates); causes oral burning and drooling
care.note: Tolerates missed waterings and low light; one of the most forgiving trailing houseplants

plants.name: Sedeveria
plants.idNote: Rosettes on stems - some Sedum/Echeveria hybrid.

care.light: Bright light with direct sun
care.water: Soak-and-dry
care.catNote: Both parents (Sedum, Echeveria) are non-toxic per ASPCA.
care.note: Dropped leaves root wherever they land - free plants.

care.light: Bright sun brings out the red
care.water: Soak-and-dry; light in winter
care.catNote: Crassula are toxic to cats per ASPCA.
care.note: More sun means redder pagodas.

care.humidity: Average humidity ok; likes a boost, avoid dry drafts
care.light: Bright indirect light; no hot midday sun
care.water: Water when top 2-3 cm dry; much less in winter
care.catNote: Toxic to cats (Ficus sap contains ficin/ficusin); irritates mouth, skin, and gut
care.note: One of the easiest bonsai, but it drops leaves when moved or hit by cold drafts

care.light: Low to medium indirect light; direct sun scorches
care.water: Keep consistently moist; never let it fully dry
care.catNote: Non-toxic to cats per ASPCA
care.note: Famously 'faints' dramatically when thirsty, then revives within hours of watering

plants.name: Mystery Rosette Seedlings
plants.idNote: Narrow-leaved rosettes in the handmade pot - dianthus seedlings, perhaps?

care.light: Full sun, 6-8 hours
care.water: Keep soil moist; water deeply when top inch dries
care.catNote: ASPCA lists basil as non-toxic to cats.
care.note: Pinch tops and flower buds often for bushier plants; hates temps below 50F.

care.light: Bright light; morning sun is ideal
care.water: Water when dry; leaves wrinkle when thirsty
care.catNote: Non-toxic to cats per ASPCA.
care.note: Extremely brittle - every fallen leaf is a future plant.

care.light: Full sun to part shade
care.water: Medium; drought tolerant once established
care.catNote: Not listed as toxic by the ASPCA; generally considered cat-safe despite saponins in the roots.
care.note: Buds inflate like little balloons before popping open; shoots emerge late in spring, so be patient.

care.humidity: Average to dry rooms fine; skip misting to avoid fungus
care.light: Bright indirect; tolerates a little direct sun
care.water: Semi-succulent; let soil nearly dry out between drinks
care.catNote: Non-toxic to cats per ASPCA (Peperomia genus is cat-safe)
care.note: Fuzzy leaves are green on top, wine-red beneath; stores water so it forgives forgetfulness

plants.name: Gourd Vine
plants.idNote: Huge fuzzy leaves racing up the balcony window.

care.light: Full sun, 6-8 hours
care.water: Thirsty; deep, steady water, big pots dry out fast
care.catNote: ASPCA lists squashes (Cucurbita) as non-toxic to cats.
care.note: On a porch, hand-pollinate morning flowers with a brush if bees are scarce.

care.light: Full sun
care.water: Deep but infrequent; dry out fully between waterings
care.catNote: Opuntia is non-toxic to cats per ASPCA, but barbed glochid spines can injure paws and mouths.
care.note: Young pads (nopales) are edible; handle with tongs since glochids detach at the lightest touch.

care.humidity: Low; dry indoor air is fine
care.light: Bright light with several hours of direct sun
care.water: Soak and dry; water only when soil is fully dry
care.catNote: Toxic per ASPCA; jade plants cause vomiting, depression, and incoordination in cats.
care.note: Tubular 'Shrek ear' leaves blush red in strong sun; cut water way back in winter.

care.light: Bright indirect light with gentle morning sun
care.water: Sparse; let soil dry completely, rots easily
care.catNote: Toxic per ASPCA; causes vomiting and lethargy, so hang it well out of feline reach.
care.note: Wrinkled pearls signal thirst; shallow roots rot fast, so use a shallow pot and gritty mix.

care.light: Full sun, 6-8 hours
care.water: Deep, consistent watering; uneven moisture causes blossom end rot
care.catNote: ASPCA lists tomato plant as toxic to cats; solanine in green parts, ripe fruit is safe.
care.note: Determinate varieties do best in pots; feed regularly, as containers leach nutrients.

care.light: Bright indirect; no hot midday sun
care.water: Weekly when bark and roots dry; never soggy
care.catNote: Phalaenopsis orchids are listed as non-toxic to cats by the ASPCA.
care.note: Silvery roots mean it's thirsty; after bloom, cut the spike above a node to coax a rebloom.

care.humidity: Average home humidity fine; enjoys occasional misting
care.light: Low to medium indirect light; no direct sun
care.water: Keep lightly moist; let top 2-3 cm dry, avoid soggy soil
care.catNote: Non-toxic to cats per ASPCA
care.note: A Victorian-era favorite that tolerates low light and neglect; overwatering is its main killer

care.light: Bright indirect; rotate weekly to keep it symmetrical
care.water: Let top 2-3 cm dry between waterings
care.catNote: Non-toxic to cats per ASPCA (Pilea genus is cat-safe)
care.note: Produces baby 'pups' around the pot, earning its pass-along 'friendship plant' reputation

plants.name: New Guinea Impatiens
plants.idNote: ID'd from the bronze foliage - flowers will tell.

care.light: Part shade; morning sun or filtered light
care.water: Consistently moist; wilts fast if it dries out
care.catNote: Impatiens are listed as non-toxic to cats by the ASPCA.
care.note: Handles more sun than common impatiens and resists downy mildew, but never let it dry out.

care.light: Full sun to light shade
care.water: Keep soil evenly moist; don't let it bake dry
care.catNote: Scarlet sage is listed as non-toxic to cats by the ASPCA.
care.note: A hummingbird magnet; deadhead spent flower spikes for color until frost.

care.light: Bright indirect light keeps the pink color
care.water: Let top of soil dry between waterings
care.catNote: Not on ASPCA list, but its sap is known to cause dermatitis and GI upset in cats and dogs.
care.note: Leaves fade from pink to plain green in dim light; pinch tips often to keep it dense.

plants.name: Stonecrop 'Autumn Joy'
plants.idNote: Nursery tag: Stonecrop 'Autumn Joy' ('Herbstfreude').

care.humidity: Low; average outdoor air is fine
care.light: Full sun
care.water: Drought tolerant; water only when soil dries
care.catNote: Sedum/stonecrop is listed as non-toxic to cats by the ASPCA.
care.note: Leave dried flower heads standing for winter interest; overly rich soil makes stems flop.

care.light: Low to medium indirect light; direct sun scorches
care.water: Keep consistently moist; never let it fully dry
care.catNote: Non-toxic to cats per ASPCA
care.note: Famously 'faints' dramatically when thirsty, then revives within hours of watering

care.light: Bright indirect light; no direct sun
care.water: Keep lightly moist; water when top 2-3 cm dry
care.catNote: Non-toxic to cats per ASPCA (listed as False Aralia, Dizygotheca elegantissima)
care.note: Drops leaves at drafts, cold, moves, or watering swings; keep conditions steady

plants.name: Pineapple Lily
plants.idNote: Big bulb + strap leaves + pineapple-shaped bloom.

care.light: Full sun, 6+ hours
care.water: Regular in summer; keep nearly dry when dormant
care.catNote: Not on ASPCA lists; saponin-rich bulbs may cause GI upset, so keep cats away to be safe.
care.note: Flower spikes topped with leafy tufts really do look like pineapples; bulbs need a dry winter rest.

plants.name: Moon Valley Pilea
plants.idNote: Costa Farms tag: 'Moon Valley Pilea'.

care.humidity: High (60%+); ideal in terrariums or on pebble trays
care.light: Medium to bright indirect light
care.water: Keep evenly moist; let just the surface dry slightly
care.catNote: Non-toxic to cats per ASPCA (friendship plant/Pilea listed as safe)
care.note: Quilted chartreuse leaves look like moon craters; shrivels fast in dry rooms

plants.name: Peperomia 'Rosso'
plants.idNote: Lives in the crocheted hanger.

care.light: Medium to bright indirect light
care.water: Let top 2-3 cm dry; sensitive to overwatering
care.catNote: Non-toxic to cats per ASPCA (listed as Emerald Ripple Peperomia, P. caperata)
care.note: Dark rippled leaves with red undersides; sends up quirky rat-tail flower spikes

care.light: Medium to bright indirect; avoid direct midday sun
care.water: Let top 2-5 cm dry between waterings
care.catNote: Non-toxic to cats per ASPCA, though cats love chewing it and may get mild GI upset
care.note: Fluoride in tap water causes brown tips; 'Bonnie' has fun curly leaves and makes babies

care.humidity: High; mist or use a pebble tray
care.light: Bright light with some direct sun for blooms
care.water: Keep soil evenly moist year-round
care.catNote: ASPCA lists chenille (Acalypha) as toxic to cats: drooling, vomiting, diarrhea.
care.note: Fuzzy red 'cat tail' catkins bloom nearly year-round; pinch off faded ones to encourage more.

care.humidity: Average home humidity fine; occasional misting appreciated
care.light: Bright indirect; more light deepens the burgundy color
care.water: Let top 3-5 cm dry between thorough waterings
care.catNote: Toxic to cats per ASPCA (ficin and ficusin in milky sap); GI and skin irritation
care.note: Wipe the big leaves so they can breathe; milky sap can irritate skin when pruning

plants.name: Blue Star Juniper
plants.idNote: Currently hosting two felt birds.

care.humidity: Fine in dry air; wants good air circulation
care.light: Full sun
care.water: Well-drained; drought tolerant once established, water in dry spells
care.catNote: Not on ASPCA lists; junipers can cause GI upset if nibbled, so treat as unsafe.
care.note: Very slow growing and cold hardy; can overwinter outside in a pot in the Northeast.

plants.name: Pinks
plants.idNote: Store label reads DIANTHUS.

care.light: Full sun
care.water: Moderate; well-drained soil, avoid soggy crowns
care.catNote: ASPCA lists pinks/carnations (Dianthus) as toxic to cats: mild GI upset and dermatitis.
care.note: Flowers smell of cloves; shear plants after the first flush for a repeat bloom.
